core_obligations: For beta in CH_{k+1}(W) introduce the closed immersion i_0 of the fibre over 0 and show (W_infinity -> X)_* i_infinity^* beta = i_0^* beta in CH_k(X), using that the two pushforwards i_{infinity,*}i_infinity^* beta and i_{0,*}i_0^* beta agree on W (proof lines 10138-10144).

Show that the restriction of beta to b^{-1}(A^1_X) restricts to the flat pullback of i_0^* beta = (W_infinity -> X)_* i_infinity^* beta, which is checked after pulling back along i_0 by the line bundle lemmas (proof lines 10145-10149).

Conclude that the chosen beta is admissible in the computation of C applied to (W_infinity -> X)_* i_infinity^* beta, giving C o (W_infinity -> X)_* o i_infinity^* = i_infinity^* (proof lines 10150-10152).
proof_roadmap: Identify the pushforward from infinity with the Gysin pullback at zero (proof lines 10138-10144).
Check that beta is admissible for that class by the line bundle lemmas (proof lines 10145-10149).
Read off the operator identity (proof lines 10150-10152).
difficulty_reason: Building on the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, the statement is the operator identity C o (W_infinity -> X)_* o i_infinity^* = i_infinity^* (statement lines 10131-10135). The proof reduces it to a single cycle class beta of W: it introduces the closed immersion i_0 of the fibre over 0 and shows that (W_infinity -> X)_* i_infinity^* beta = i_0^* beta in CH_k(X), because i_{infinity,*}i_infinity^* beta and i_{0,*}i_0^* beta represent the same class on W and hence push forward to the same class on X (proof lines 10138-10144). The remaining point is that beta is an admissible input for computing C applied to the pushed forward class: the restriction of beta to b^{-1}(A^1_X) restricts to the flat pullback of i_0^* beta = (W_infinity -> X)_* i_infinity^* beta, which may be checked after pulling back along i_0 by the two line bundle lemmas (proof lines 10145-10152). Recognising that the two boundary divisors give the same class on W and that this makes the same beta serve in the definition of C is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
